episode.title: [Bug]: Multiplex: API-server turns for different profiles share one Docker sandbox when their opening messages match
episode.before: Before b5f587dba8b1852127c6cc3d7e3d98dceedbf94d, the parent implementation used the alias-resolved raw task/session id directly for a session-isolated backend. A multiplexed process serving multiple profiles could therefore put identical header-less API-server fingerprints into the same _active_environments slot: the second profile could attach to the first profile's sandbox, including its image, mounts, and exported environment. The separate session-cwd map also indexed record, read, and clear operations by the raw id, so one profile could overwrite, read, or clear another profile's working-directory state. There was no shared profile/home qualifier for these raw-id paths, although ordinary no-override behavior was intentionally raw-keyed.
episode.after: After the change, a context-local routed home/profile scope is converted into a stable qualifier: named profiles use a profile-qualified prefix, the canonical default uses profile:default, and otherwise the active home realpath is used, with an error-safe textual fallback. Session-isolated task ids are alias-resolved and then qualified before they index the active environment cache; with no routed override they remain raw. The session-cwd record, get, and clear operations apply the same qualification symmetrically, so identical raw ids in different routed profiles use independent cwd slots. Existing persistent-Docker profile-key branches and ordinary single-profile/no-override raw-key behavior remain unchanged.
episode.diff: The parent-to-commit diff changes exactly two files. In tools/terminal_tool.py it adds the routed home qualifier and generic task-key qualification helper, applies qualification to the session-isolated container-key branch, and changes the session-cwd record/get/clear trio to use the same helper; the terminal call-site comment documents that the centralized functions keep worker-thread callers symmetric. In tests/tools/test_docker_session_isolation.py it adds the TestRoutedScopeQualification regression class with six tests covering legacy no-override behavior, named-profile qualification, identical fingerprint collisions across named and default profiles, subagent alias qualification, symmetric cwd isolation/clear behavior, and raw cwd storage without an override. The implementation portion is 61 insertions and 7 deletions; the test addition is 98 lines.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned commit subject explicitly says it qualifies session-isolated container keys and cwd records under a routed profile scope. Its commit narrative identifies the collision mechanism: identical opening messages can produce the same fingerprint-derived API session id, causing two profiles to share one session-isolated environment cache slot; it also states the intended preservation of raw CLI/single-profile behavior and persistent-Docker profile labels.

The pinned ref changes exactly tests/tools/test_docker_session_isolation.py and tools/terminal_tool.py. The diff statistics are 98 added test lines and 61 added/7 deleted implementation lines, for 159 insertions and 7 deletions overall.
evidence_units.source: git diff --stat and git diff --numstat 2e3c9ceeb1cfca90f8d5a6eea3210dd78c86846f b5f587dba8b1852127c6cc3d7e3d98dceedbf94d

evidence_units.claim: In the parent, record_session_cwd stored str(session_key or default) directly, get_session_cwd read that raw key, and clear_session_cwd popped the raw key. In the parent session-isolated branch, _resolve_container_task_id returned _resolve_container_alias(task_id) directly, so a routed profile was absent from both the environment-cache key and cwd-record key.

The shared session-scope predicate treats Docker with a nonpersistent setting and plugin backends declaring session_isolated_when_nonpersistent as session-isolated when persistence is false. The changed container-key branch therefore covers the backend class described by the commit, while Docker-specific mount/lifecycle predicates remain separate.

The implementation adds _home_scope_qualifier and _qualify_task_key. With no active home override the qualifier is empty; with an override, profile_name_for_home maps the canonical default to profile:default, a named profile to profile:<name>, and an otherwise unclassified home to home:<realpath>, falling back to the override string if realpath raises OSError. _qualify_task_key prefixes only when a qualifier exists.

The session-isolated container branch now returns _qualify_task_key(_resolve_container_alias(task_id)). The alias is resolved before qualification, preserving the parent-container relationship for subagents while placing the resulting key in the active routed profile/home namespace. The image/env-type override branch remains earlier and authoritative, and the persistent-Docker branches are not changed by this patch.

record_session_cwd, get_session_cwd, and clear_session_cwd all use _qualify_task_key at their storage boundary. This makes write, read, and teardown use the same scoped slot instead of allowing a profile's read or clear operation to address another profile's raw-id record.

Existing callers continue to use the centralized cwd and environment-key APIs: task override registration records cwd and cleanup clears it; command cwd resolution and environment planning read the session cwd; environment acquisition resolves the effective container key; and terminal result processing records observed cwd. The patch therefore fixes the shared state boundary without editing each consumer.
evidence_units.source: tools/terminal_tool.py:323-355, 949-976, 1136-1149, 1431-1443; repository-wide rg call-site search for record_session_cwd, get_session_cwd, clear_session_cwd, and _resolve_container_task_id

evidence_units.claim: The added TestRoutedScopeQualification tests assert that no override preserves a raw API key and raw cwd map key; a named routed profile yields profile:research:api-abc123; the same raw fingerprint in research and default profiles yields distinct keys; a routed subagent alias resolves to a qualified parent; profile B starts with no profile A cwd record, can clear only its own record, and profile A's record remains; and cwd storage is raw without an override.

The commit message reports that the routed-scope regression tests fail on the pre-fix implementation for 4 of 6 tests and pass after the fix, that live Docker verification exercised both profile directions, and that persistent-Docker behavior remained byte-identical with profile/default labels.

candidate_atomics.name: derive_routed_scope_qualifier
candidate_atomics.description: Derive a stable namespace component from the active routed profile/home context, with an empty result when no routed override is active so legacy identity remains intact.

semantic_action.intent: Provide a profile/home discriminator for mutable terminal state when one process serves multiple routed scopes.
semantic_action.pre_state: Raw terminal state keys have no common scope component, even when a call is executing under a context-local routed home override; calls without an override must retain the historical unqualified identity.
semantic_action.post_state: The active scope yields profile:default for the canonical default, profile:<name> for a named profile, or home:<realpath> with a safe textual fallback for an otherwise unclassified home; no override yields an empty qualifier.
semantic_action.validation: The routed-profile key test observes the profile-qualified result and the no-override tests observe the unchanged raw result. The helper is validated indirectly through its container-key and cwd-state consumers rather than by a direct helper-only test.

candidate_atomics.name: qualify_session_isolated_container_key
candidate_atomics.description: Namespace the alias-resolved task identity used for a session-isolated sandbox by the active routed profile/home, preventing same-fingerprint profiles from sharing an environment cache slot while preserving subagent aliasing and legacy raw behavior.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent cross-profile reuse of a session-isolated sandbox when different profiles generate the same raw API-session fingerprint.
semantic_action.pre_state: For a session-isolated backend, the alias-resolved raw task id is used directly as the environment-cache identity, so identical raw ids from different routed profiles can attach to one sandbox.
semantic_action.post_state: The alias-resolved task identity is prefixed by the active routed scope, making equal raw ids from different profiles distinct; subagent aliases still resolve to the parent's qualified identity, while no routed override keeps the raw key and earlier explicit isolation overrides remain authoritative.
semantic_action.validation: The regression tests prove named-profile qualification, distinct keys for a research/default fingerprint collision, qualified subagent-parent resolution, and raw behavior without an override. The commit also reports live Docker isolation in both profile directions.

candidate_atomics.name: qualify_session_cwd_state
candidate_atomics.description: Apply the same routed scope qualification to session working-directory record, lookup, and teardown operations so cwd state cannot cross profile boundaries or be cleared asymmetrically.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent cross-profile working-directory state bleed for equal raw session ids and preserve symmetric cleanup.
semantic_action.pre_state: The cwd map records, reads, and clears by raw session id, so a profile sharing the id can observe or overwrite another profile's directory and can clear its record.
semantic_action.post_state: Record, get, and clear all address the same scope-qualified slot; a different routed profile sees no prior record, owns its own cwd, and can clear only that slot, while no override continues to use the raw slot.
semantic_action.validation: The cwd regression test records profile A's directory, verifies profile B starts empty, records and clears B, and then verifies A remains unchanged; a separate no-override assertion verifies raw map storage.

candidate_workflows.name: routed_profile_terminal_isolation
candidate_workflows.description: Establish one reusable routed-scope namespace and apply it to the two mutable terminal state boundaries implicated by the collision: session-isolated environment identities and session cwd records.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure profiles served by one process cannot share a session-isolated sandbox or cwd record merely because their raw API-session fingerprints match, while preserving unqualified single-profile behavior.
workflow_graph.entry_state: One process serves routed profiles A and B; identical opening messages can produce the same raw session id, and raw per-session environment and cwd state are profile-blind.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The same raw id resolves to distinct environment identities and independent cwd slots under different routed profiles; no-override behavior remains raw and persistent-Docker profile scoping remains stable.
